title: Black Sesame Custard Ice Cream
changes_from_base: Brown sugar instead of caster, one more yolk, less dairy, and black sesame paste whisked in after cooking; no vanilla.
summary: Based on our classic custard method, this has brown sugar in place of caster, one extra yolk and a generous amount of black sesame paste whisked in after cooking. Deeply nutty with a striking grey colour.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk the brown sugar, yolks and salt together in the saucepan, then whisk in the cream and milk.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Heat over medium-low until warm, then raise to medium and keep stirring with the spatula until steaming and 77-80 °C, about 10 min. Do not let it bubble.

steps.title: Add the sesame
steps.text: Off the heat, whisk in the black sesame paste until smooth and strain into a bowl. A quick buzz with a stick blender gives a more even colour.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Set the bowl in the iced water, stirring from time to time, for about 30 min, then cover and refrigerate for at least 4 h.

steps.title: Churn
steps.text: Chill the container and a spatula in the freezer while the ice cream churns until fluffy and thick.

steps.title: Freeze
steps.text: Scrape into the cold container, press baking paper onto the surface and freeze for about 4 h.

tips: Use unsweetened Japanese-style black sesame paste; sweetened pastes will make it too sweet.
A common mistake is adding the paste before cooking, which makes the custard hard to judge. Stir it in afterwards.
Serve with fresh figs or a drizzle of honey.
storage: Freeze, covered, for up to 2 weeks.
